header:
Mg-Air Batteries
With their high specific energy density, stable operating voltage, simple device construction, and excellent safety, magnesium-air batteries have become candidates for emergency backup power in hospitals, emergency power for disaster relief, portable field energy-storage devices, and automotive power supplies.

subquestions.text_open: 6-2-3 In practical use, additional Ca is incorporated into the Mg alloy. Explain why. (K_{sp}[Ca(OH)_2] = 5.5 × 10^{-6})

6-3 Investigation of second-phase effects

Alloying is an effective means of modifying materials and can significantly improve the discharge performance of magnesium alloys. The type, morphology, and distribution of the second phase, i.e., another phase distributed discontinuously within the matrix phase, directly affect material performance. When a new metal is added to the base electrode material during alloy-electrode manufacture, a second phase forms. Microgalvanic couples between the second phase and matrix phase undergo galvanic corrosion. Galvanic corrosion occurs when two different metals are in contact while simultaneously exposed to an electrolyte, forming a spontaneous cell in which the more active metal acts as the anode and corrodes. The rate of galvanic corrosion depends on the contact area between the two metals.

6-3-1 The anode efficiency is calculated as $P = \frac{W_f}{\Delta W}$, where $\Delta W$ is the actual mass loss and $W_f$ is the theoretical mass loss, calculated from $W_f = \frac{I \times t}{F \times \sum\limits_{i=1}^{n} \frac{X_i \times N_i}{M_i}}$. Here, $F$ is the Faraday constant, $X_i$ is the mass fraction of each element in the magnesium anode, $N_i$ is the corresponding number of electrons transferred by each element in the electrochemical process, and $M_i$ is the atomic mass of each element.

Alloy materials A and B have the following compositions:

| Alloy material | La | Ce | Ca | Al | Zn | Mg |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | / | / | / | 6% | 3% | 91% |
| B | 0.15% | 0.45% | 0.3% | 6% | 3% | 90.1% |

For $\Delta W$, $\Delta W_A = 36.27\,\text{mg}$ and $\Delta W_B = 30.01\,\text{mg}$. Calculate the anode efficiencies of A and B at a current density of $0.5\,\text{mA/cm}^2$, duration of $6\,\text{h}$, and area of $14\,\text{cm}^2$.

6-3-2 Subsequent research proposed that the difference in efficiency between alloy materials A and B originates from a change in the second phase. After addition of the new metals, the second phase changes from the particulate and planar morphologies in A to the rod-like and relatively continuous β-Mg_{17}Al_{12}/τ-Mg_{32}(Al, Zn)_{49} and Al_{2}(La, Ce) structures in B. Explain the difference in efficiency on this basis.
